Subject: Bake-off test plan: Redwood vs hyperscaler APIs — proposed scope & owners

Hi Maria — great to meet today. Thanks for the time and for walking us through your latency and inference-cost concerns for the control software pipeline. Per our discussion, I put together a lean bake-off plan so we can get aligned on scope, success criteria, and owners. Attached a fillable template (bakeoff_template.xlsx) and a short summary of Redwood perf characteristics (redwood_perf_summary.pdf).

Summary of discovery highlights (quick):
- Primary goal: choose an inference provider for low-latency command-generation and telemetry synthesis (real-time loop).
- Constraints: p95 latency SLO ~< 200ms for 512-token responses; burst throughput peaks at 80 concurrent sessions; strict audit logging requirement for model inputs/outputs.
- Current comparison targets: AWS Bedrock (distro of open models), Google Vertex AI endpoints, and a third-party inference API your team is evaluating.

Proposed bake-off scope (suggested minimum matrix):
1) Baseline hosted API comparison: Redwood hosted vs Bedrock vs Vertex — same model family where possible, default quantization. Metrics: latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput (concurrency), cost per 1k tokens, correctness on canonical prompt set.
2) Dedicated capacity test: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU) for throughput and cold-start behavior.
3) Feature checks: streaming output, function/tool calling fidelity, KV-cache warm vs cold, prefix caching impact.
4) Security/compliance: evidence of audit logs, KMS integration, VPC peering options for private testing.

Success criteria (draft):
- Latency: p95 <= 200ms on 512-token typical prompts during steady-state throughput test (80 concurrent).
- Cost: total cost per 1M tokens delivered <= target you set during procurement (we should confirm target $/token).
- Quality: >=95% pass rate on your acceptance prompts (we'll need an eval set from your team).
- Integration: streaming and function-calling work end-to-end with <50ms chunking latency.

Proposed owners & timeline:
- Ben Carter (me) — commercial lead, coord, logistics, credits/contract follow-up.
- Marissa Cole — solutions lead, responsible for test harness and running experiments.
- Rishi Malhotra — security/compliance owner (handles KMS, audit log artifacts, VPC options).
- Laura Bennett — sales engineering escalation and resource approvals.

Timeline (rough):
- This week (by 2026-08-07): finalize eval prompt set and success thresholds (owner: Acme + Ben).
- Week of 2026-08-10: Marissa to run baseline hosted comparisons (3 providers).
- Week of 2026-08-17: Dedicated capacity throughput tests and security evidence collection (Rishi + Marissa).
- 2026-08-24: Results review + decision checkpoint.

Next steps I propose:
1) Maria, share a 30–50 prompt eval set and your cost target for 1M tokens by Friday.
2) We kick off a 30-min technical kickoff Tue or Wed to align on test harness and VPC needs.
3) I'll provision a temporary Redwood Dedicated sandbox and allocate credits for the run.

If this looks good, I can schedule the kickoff and loop in engineering. Attaching the template and the perf blurb.

Thanks — looking forward to proving out the performance.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
